verdict.rationale: LiteLLM Proxy issues virtual keys that restrict which models a credential can call (docs-8), carry per-key budgets and reset periods (docs-7, docs-25, docs-35) and rate limits (docs-26), and gate MCP tool access by key or team (docs-14). Together these let an agent receive a least-privilege credential, and key-scoped guardrails extend this in the enterprise tier (docs-37). The single community complaint about issues creating tokens for other users is too vague to dispute the capability, but it lowers confidence. Missing for 10: documented key expiry/rotation and fine-grained per-endpoint permissions, agent-specific credential guidance, guardrail scoping outside the enterprise tier, and independent hands-on corroboration of key scoping.
